claim: Parameter-based knowledge editing cannot reliably update factual knowledge in a large language model without damaging its core capabilities. The near-perfect editing results reported in prior work do not survive realistic evaluation, and the limitation is geometric rather than incidental: localized weight edits are disproportionately amplified along low-variance directions of the model's representation space and propagate globally, so damage compounds as edits accumulate. A parameter-free approach that leaves the weights untouched is therefore a serious alternative to parameter editing rather than a fallback.
experiments_evaluated: To address subclaim 1, subclaim 2, and subclaim 6, run a realistic sequential-edit benchmark comparing parameter-based editors (ROME, MEND, KE, constrained fine-tuning) against parameter-free baselines (IKE and, if available, a retrieval/memory editor that leaves base weights untouched) on GPT-2 and GPT-J using public COUNTERFACT and ZSRE splits. First filter to editable/nontrivial cases as standard in the field. Evaluate single-edit rollback and then cumulative no-rollback settings with batch/sequential counts 1, 10, 100, and 1000 edits. For each condition report Reliability/ES on edited prompts, Generalization/PS on paraphrases, Locality/NS on out-of-scope prompts, plus capability preservation on HellaSwag, LAMBADA, and Natural Questions, and optionally perplexity on held-out text. Include pre-edit baselines, in-context editing baselines, and cross-dataset replication. The key test is whether the near-perfect single-edit results survive once edits accumulate and broader capabilities are measured. If parameter editors maintain high Reliability while keeping Locality and external task performance near pre-edit levels across edit counts, the main claim is weakened. If apparent success collapses under sequential evaluation or broad-task checks while parameter-free methods remain competitive or more stable, that supports the claim that prior near-perfect reports do not survive realistic evaluation and that damage compounds with accumulation. If strong results appear only in rollback/single-edit settings, one can conclude the limitation is practical even if isolated edits look good. This experiment becomes less necessary if there already exists a large, independently replicated benchmark covering sequential no-rollback edits, out-of-scope locality, and unrelated capability retention across multiple editors and backbones.

To address subclaim 3, subclaim 4, and subclaim 5, perform a representation-geometry and propagation analysis around edits on GPT-J and GPT-2 using COUNTERFACT facts localized by both causal tracing and representation zeroing. For each editable fact, identify the edit site via the standard layer/token sweep, then record pre-edit hidden-state covariance at the relevant layer over a large public text sample. After applying a localized weight edit (e.g., ROME or MEMIT-style single-fact update if available, otherwise ROME/KE), decompose the induced change in hidden states and logits into principal-component directions of the pre-edit representation space. Quantify whether edit-induced deltas are disproportionately aligned with low-variance PCs relative to random matched-norm parameter perturbations and small constrained fine-tuning updates. Separately, measure propagation by tracing activation/logit changes across all layers, tokens, and a held-out unrelated prompt set, not just the edited prompt, and regress downstream behavior change on alignment with low-variance directions while controlling for edited layer and update norm. If edits consistently project more strongly onto low-variance directions than controls, and those directions predict larger global activation/output shifts on unrelated prompts, that supports the geometric-amplification account rather than an incidental implementation artifact. If instead edit effects mostly live in high-variance or local directions and unrelated prompts remain unaffected once norm and layer are controlled, the geometric claim is weakened. If propagation is observed only for particular layers or one localization method, the conclusion should be narrowed accordingly. This experiment could be partly obviated by prior public evidence showing the same low-variance amplification and global propagation across multiple architectures, localization procedures, and editor families.

To address subclaim 7 and subclaim 8, compare parameter-free and parameter-modifying editing under matched utility and cost constraints. Use the same editable subset from COUNTERFACT and ZSRE, the same backbones (GPT-2, GPT-J), and methods including IKE plus any public parameter-preserving memory/adaptor editor available, versus ROME, MEND, KE, and fine-tuning. Verify subclaim 7 directly by auditing trainable/base-weight changes: hash and diff model checkpoints before/after editing, report edited parameters and extra parameters, and confirm whether methods leave base weights untouched or instead add external memory/modules. Then test whether the parameter-free approach is a serious alternative by evaluating the full quality profile: Reliability/ES, Generalization/PS, Locality/NS, sequential stability over many edits, inference latency, memory footprint, and robustness-task retention on HellaSwag/LAMBADA/NQ. Also include an in-context prompting baseline to separate pure prompt effects from more structured parameter-free editing. If parameter-free methods leave base weights unchanged and achieve similar or better edit quality/stability tradeoffs than parameter editors, especially under sequential and robustness evaluation, that supports the claim that they are a serious alternative rather than merely a fallback. If they preserve weights but perform much worse on reliability/generalization at comparable resource budgets, then they may be best viewed as a fallback. If simple in-context prompting matches them, one may conclude the advantage comes from generic prompting rather than a distinct editing paradigm. This experiment would be less necessary if there is already a standardized public benchmark with checkpoint audits and matched-cost comparisons showing parameter-free methods are consistently competitive across datasets and edit volumes.
reference_experiments: Fix the measurement floor and the inference protocol before editing anything. Score the unedited model on the editing benchmark to establish the pre-edit baseline, and re-run single-edit evaluation of existing methods under plain autoregressive decoding rather than the teacher-forced protocol prior work used, since teacher forcing supplies the ground-truth answer tokens at inference and inflates every number. If methods keep their near-perfect single-edit scores under honest decoding there is no discrepancy to explain. The authors report a pre-edit baseline of Reliability 3.00, Generalization 3.00, Locality 15.50, Portability 4.36 on ZsRE, and a best parameter-based single-edit average of 25.99.

Validate the scoring instrument before quoting any number from it. Judge semantic consistency of generated answers with a strong LLM across reliability, generalization, locality and portability, then cross-check that ranking with a deterministic token-level measure (match ratio and exact match) that does not depend on a model's opinion. If the two disagree, every result is an artifact of the judge rather than a property of the editing methods. The authors find the token-level check reproduces the semantic ranking, with the pre-edit model at 100% by definition and GRACE holding 100% under both single and sequential editing.

Test the asserted mechanism directly. Take the SVD of the original hidden-representation matrix, compute the directional relative change rate R_k = sqrt(n)|u_k^T delta_h| / sigma_k for each principal direction after an edit, and check where amplification concentrates and how it behaves as edits accumulate. The claim's causal story requires R_k > 1 predominantly in low-singular-value directions with the fraction rising monotonically with edit count, across methods and architectures.

Run the main benchmark. Compare eleven editing methods spanning locate-then-edit (ROME, MEMIT, PMET, RECT, AlphaEdit, FT-L), meta-learning (MEND), additional-parameter (AdaLoRA, WISE) and external-memory (GRACE, SCR) families, under sequential editing at 1, 10, 100 and full-dataset edit counts, on ZsRE and WikiData-counterfact, across Llama-2-7B-Chat, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Mistral-7B-Instruct and DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B, reporting all four dimensions. The claim holds if every parameter-modifying method degrades toward zero as edits accumulate and the parameter-free retrieval baseline outscores all of them; the authors report ROME, RECT, FT-L, MEND and AdaLoRA at 0.00-0.25 average under sequential editing on DeepSeek-R1-Distill, against SCR at 56.59 single and 60.19 sequential.

Measure damage to capabilities the edits never targeted. Take the models edited in the main benchmark and evaluate them on mathematical reasoning (AIME 2024, AIME 2025, AMC, OlympiadBench, MATH-500) and broad benchmarks (GPQA-Diamond, ARC-c, MMLU-Pro), reporting accuracy after 10 and after 100 sequential edits. Without this the study would only show editing is ineffective, not that it is damaging. The authors report ROME and RECT losing 2.74 and 8.37 average accuracy at 10 edits and falling to near zero at 100, with MEND at 0.00 after both.

Rule out that the result is an artifact of scale, knowledge type, fact difficulty or one method's configuration. Repeat the sweep on larger models (Llama-2-13B, Qwen3-14B), on event-level knowledge (ELKEN, with events converted to triples for the parameter-based arms), split by high- and low-confidence fact sets, and probe the hyperparameter and architecture sensitivity of AlphaEdit — the one method that does not collapse — including its failure to run on Llama-2 and Mistral. If the collapse disappears at 13-14B or only occurs on triple-shaped facts, the claim is bounded rather than general.

reference_coverage.adequacy: An unedited baseline and a free-running single-edit comparison that can distinguish genuine performance from inflation caused by supplying answer tokens during evaluation.
reference_coverage.rationale: Proposed experiment 0 includes pre-edit baselines, an explicit single-edit condition, realistic generation-based editing metrics, and cumulative no-rollback evaluation. It therefore gives the team the clean reference point and the isolated-versus-sequential comparison needed to test whether apparently near-perfect editing survives an honest protocol.

reference_coverage.adequacy: Convergent evidence from a semantic assessment and an independent deterministic token-level assessment, allowing method rankings to be checked for dependence on the evaluator.
reference_coverage.rationale: The proposed experiments report editing-quality measures such as Reliability/ES and Generalization/PS, but they do not require a semantic judge and a deterministic token-level scorer to be applied to the same outputs, nor do they specify an agreement or ranking cross-check. They can measure performance, but cannot establish that any observed ranking is independent of the scoring instrument.
reasoning_chain: The reference experiment establishes whether the apparent editing result survives agreement between model-based semantic scoring and deterministic token scoring.
The proposed set reports quality metrics but does not require those two independent scoring families or a direct consistency analysis.
A strong or weak result could therefore still be attributable to the chosen scorer rather than the editing method.
The team would fail to learn whether the reported method ranking is scorer-independent.

reference_coverage.adequacy: A causal, normalized measurement of edit-induced representation change relative to native variance, tested across directions, repeated edit loads, methods and architectures, and linked to downstream global propagation.
reference_coverage.rationale: Proposed experiment 1 directly tests low-variance principal-component alignment, uses matched-norm perturbation controls, and measures activation/logit propagation on unrelated prompts. Proposed experiment 0 separately tests behavioral degradation over edit counts. However, experiment 1 is described around a localized single-fact update and does not require measuring the native-scale-normalized directional change after repeated edits or testing a monotonic increase with edit count. The set can establish low-variance association, propagation, and behavioral accumulation, but leaves ambiguous whether the normalized geometric amplification itself compounds as edits accumulate.
reasoning_chain: The reference mechanism requires relative amplification against the native signal scale and accumulation across repeated edits, not merely directional alignment after one edit.
The proposed geometry study records covariance and compares low-variance alignment with matched-norm controls, but does not specify repeated geometric measurements or a monotonic edit-count test.
The proposed benchmark measures performance at multiple edit counts but does not decompose those outcomes into the directional normalized representation statistic.
The team would fail to learn whether the claimed low-variance amplification mechanism itself compounds with repeated editing.

evidence.quote: Taken together, Sections 4.2 and 4.3 suggest the following picture: dimensional collapse creates directions with extremely small native signal scales; small local edits are therefore disproportionately amplified in relative terms; and repeated editing compounds this vulnerability, eventually destabilizing the broader representation geometry.
evidence.bearing: The reference mechanism requires both native-scale-relative amplification and repeated-edit accumulation, which is why the proposed single-edit geometry analysis does not fully cover it.

reference_coverage.adequacy: A broad factorial comparison of isolated and cumulative factual-edit utility, preservation dimensions, and a weight-preserving competitor across diverse editor mechanisms, model families, datasets and edit loads.
reference_coverage.rationale: The proposed benchmark covers single and cumulative loads, two datasets, several parameter-modifying approaches, parameter-free comparisons, all four editing dimensions, and unrelated-task retention. Its evidential scope is materially narrower: it uses two closely related decoder-only backbones, a small subset of editor mechanisms, and a filtered editable/nontrivial subset, with the retrieval competitor conditional on availability. Thus it can establish the phenomenon in the tested setting but cannot distinguish a broad limitation from a failure specific to those backbones, methods, or selected cases.
reasoning_chain: The reference sweep is designed to determine whether sequential degradation and the advantage of a weight-preserving alternative persist across substantially varied methods, architectures, datasets and edit loads.

The proposed set supplies the edit-load and metric comparisons, but concentrates on GPT-2/GPT-J, a limited editor sample, and filtered cases rather than testing the broader range of model families and method types.
A collapse in that setting could consequently be a property of the selected models, editors, or selection rule rather than parameter-based editing generally.
The team would fail to learn whether the main benchmark conclusion generalizes across the broader class of large language models and editing methods.

reference_coverage.adequacy: Untargeted capability retention measured against a clean baseline on independent reasoning, language, and knowledge tasks at multiple cumulative edit loads.
reference_coverage.rationale: Proposed experiment 0 explicitly includes pre-edit baselines and capability preservation on HellaSwag, LAMBADA and Natural Questions at the same cumulative edit loads, while experiment 2 repeats robustness-task retention in the matched comparison. These independent tasks span multiple core capabilities and can show whether edits damage abilities unrelated to the edited facts; the particular benchmark names are not binding to the claim.

reference_coverage.adequacy: Stress tests that separate model scale, knowledge form, fact difficulty and editor hyperparameter or architecture sensitivity, so a failure cannot be attributed to a narrow configuration.
reference_coverage.rationale: The proposed set has some cross-dataset replication, two backbones, several editors, matched-norm controls and localization alternatives. It does not, however, include a larger-scale sweep, event-level knowledge, explicit high- versus low-confidence fact strata, or a systematic hyperparameter/architecture sensitivity analysis of the strongest surviving editor. It therefore probes generality but leaves several major alternative explanations open.
reasoning_chain: The reference experiment tests whether the reported collapse is robust to scale, knowledge type, fact difficulty and configuration rather than being a narrow benchmark artifact.

The proposed experiments vary datasets, backbones and some procedures, but do not vary event-level versus triple-like knowledge, fact-confidence strata, larger model scale, or editor sensitivity systematically.
Those omissions leave open whether the observed behavior changes under the untested knowledge forms, difficulty levels, scales or configurations.
The team would fail to learn how broadly the conclusion survives those key scope and configuration changes.

sufficiency_reasoning: Executed as written, the proposed set would provide substantial evidence for realistic sequential degradation, untargeted capability damage, global propagation, low-variance directional involvement, and a weight-preserving alternative with direct checkpoint auditing and matched utility/cost measurements. It would not fully settle the claim's strongest form because the independent semantic/token scoring validation is absent, the geometric study does not directly measure native-scale-normalized amplification across repeated edit counts, and the empirical scope is narrower than needed to rule out scale, knowledge-type, difficulty and configuration artifacts.
missing: A paired semantic-judge versus deterministic token-level scoring validation on the same outputs and conditions.
Repeated-edit representation measurements using a native-signal-normalized directional amplification statistic, with an explicit monotonic edit-count analysis.
Broader robustness sweeps over model scale and architecture families, event-level knowledge, fact-difficulty strata, and hyperparameter/configuration sensitivity of strong editors.
